t: What a Bill of Materials Is (Signature Edition)
name: What a Bill of Materials Is (Signature Edition)
title: What a Bill of Materials Is (Signature Edition)
description: Signature reading: The BoM is the build's source of truth: one product, one list, no duplicates, no mysteries. A bill of materials (BoM) is a structured list of every raw material, component, and subassembly needed to build one unit of a product. It is the single document that purchasing buys against, production picks against, and costing is calculated from.
how_it_works: Treat every BoM as a contract between design and reality: if a part is not on the BoM with a number, a quantity, and a source, it does not exist for the build. Signature practice keeps one authoritative BoM per revision and derives everything else from it.
key_points: Signature reading: The BoM is the build's source of truth: one product, one list, no duplicates, no mysteries.
One BoM describes exactly one revision of one product.
Every line needs a unique part number - never describe parts by prose alone.
Quantity-per-assembly and unit of measure are mandatory fields.
The BoM is the basis for purchasing, costing, and production planning.
requirements: A defined product structure with unique part numbers for every item; quantities and units of measure; revision control on the BoM document.
standards: IPC-1782 and IPC-2581 for electronics BoMs; ASME Y14.38 for parts lists; company part-numbering standard applied consistently.
citations: Signature build engineering readings, JAH Databases - original work, explicitly labeled as Signature originals.

name: Single-Level vs Multi-Level BoMs (Signature Edition)
title: Single-Level vs Multi-Level BoMs (Signature Edition)
description: Signature reading: Structure follows the build: if you build subassemblies separately, your BoM shows them separately. A single-level BoM lists only the parts bought or made at the top level, flattening subassemblies into their components. A multi-level (indented) BoM shows the full parent-child hierarchy, with each subassembly exploded into its own parts.
how_it_works: Treat every BoM as a contract between design and reality: if a part is not on the BoM with a number, a quantity, and a source, it does not exist for the build. Signature practice keeps one authoritative BoM per revision and derives everything else from it.
key_points: Signature reading: Structure follows the build: if you build subassemblies separately, your BoM shows them separately.
Single-level: flat list, simplest to maintain for simple products.
Multi-level: indented hierarchy showing subassemblies and their parts.
Level 0 is always the finished shippable product.
Choose the structure that matches how the product is actually built.
requirements: A defined product structure with unique part numbers for every item; quantities and units of measure; revision control on the BoM document.
standards: IPC-1782 and IPC-2581 for electronics BoMs; ASME Y14.38 for parts lists; company part-numbering standard applied consistently.

t: Quantities and Units of Measure (Signature Edition)
name: Quantities and Units of Measure (Signature Edition)
title: Quantities and Units of Measure (Signature Edition)
description: Signature reading: Count what you consume, in the unit you buy - and write the unit down. Quantity-per-assembly states how many of each part go into one parent; the unit of measure (each, feet, grams, liters) defines what the quantity counts. Mismatched units are one of the most common and expensive BoM errors.
how_it_works: Treat every BoM as a contract between design and reality: if a part is not on the BoM with a number, a quantity, and a source, it does not exist for the build. Signature practice keeps one authoritative BoM per revision and derives everything else from it.
key_points: Signature reading: Count what you consume, in the unit you buy - and write the unit down.
Every BoM line needs quantity-per-assembly AND unit of measure.
Buy-unit vs use-unit conversions must be stated, not assumed.
Fractional quantities are normal for bulk materials (0.02 liters of adhesive).
Audit units whenever a BoM is copied between metric and imperial shops.
requirements: A defined product structure with unique part numbers for every item; quantities and units of measure; revision control on the BoM document.
standards: IPC-1782 and IPC-2581 for electronics BoMs; ASME Y14.38 for parts lists; company part-numbering standard applied consistently.

name: Engineering vs Manufacturing BoMs (Signature Edition)
title: Engineering vs Manufacturing BoMs (Signature Edition)
description: Signature reading: Design organizes by function; manufacturing organizes by process - honor both with two views. The engineering BoM (EBOM) reflects how the product is designed - functional groupings from CAD. The manufacturing BoM (MBOM) reflects how it is built - process order, consumables, packaging, and phantom assemblies added.
how_it_works: Treat every BoM as a contract between design and reality: if a part is not on the BoM with a number, a quantity, and a source, it does not exist for the build. Signature practice keeps one authoritative BoM per revision and derives everything else from it.
key_points: Signature reading: Design organizes by function; manufacturing organizes by process - honor both with two views.
EBOM: as-designed structure from engineering/CAD.
MBOM: as-built structure for the production line.
MBOM adds consumables, packaging, and process steps EBOM omits.
Traceability between EBOM and MBOM lines is mandatory.
requirements: A defined product structure with unique part numbers for every item; quantities and units of measure; revision control on the BoM document.
standards: IPC-1782 and IPC-2581 for electronics BoMs; ASME Y14.38 for parts lists; company part-numbering standard applied consistently.

name: BoM Revision Control (Signature Edition)
title: BoM Revision Control (Signature Edition)
description: Signature reading: A BoM without revision control is a rumor; with it, it is a contract. BoMs change, and uncontrolled changes cause wrong parts to be ordered and built. Revision control gives every released BoM version an identifier and a change record so everyone works from the same truth.
how_it_works: Treat every BoM as a contract between design and reality: if a part is not on the BoM with a number, a quantity, and a source, it does not exist for the build. Signature practice keeps one authoritative BoM per revision and derives everything else from it.
key_points: Signature reading: A BoM without revision control is a rumor; with it, it is a contract.
Every release gets a revision identifier and a change log.
Only the current released revision is buildable.
Superseded revisions are retained for traceability, never deleted.
An engineering change order is the only legitimate way to alter a released BoM.
requirements: A defined product structure with unique part numbers for every item; quantities and units of measure; revision control on the BoM document.
standards: IPC-1782 and IPC-2581 for electronics BoMs; ASME Y14.38 for parts lists; company part-numbering standard applied consistently.

Phantoms organize the BoM without creating stock transactions.

Use for documentation groupings like fastener kits or wiring groups.

name: BoM Cost Roll-Up (Signature Edition)
title: BoM Cost Roll-Up (Signature Edition)
description: Signature reading: Cost is a property of the BoM, not a guess - roll it up from the lines. Cost roll-up multiplies each line's quantity by its unit cost and sums upward through the levels to give the product's material cost. It is the foundation of pricing, margin analysis, and make-vs-buy decisions.
how_it_works: Treat every BoM as a contract between design and reality: if a part is not on the BoM with a number, a quantity, and a source, it does not exist for the build. Signature practice keeps one authoritative BoM per revision and derives everything else from it.
key_points: Signature reading: Cost is a property of the BoM, not a guess - roll it up from the lines.
Extended cost = quantity-per-assembly x unit cost, summed per level.
Roll up from the lowest level to the top for the true material cost.
Keep material, labor, and overhead visible separately.
Re-roll costs on every BoM revision and every price change.
requirements: A defined product structure with unique part numbers for every item; quantities and units of measure; revision control on the BoM document.
standards: IPC-1782 and IPC-2581 for electronics BoMs; ASME Y14.38 for parts lists; company part-numbering standard applied consistently.

t: Approved Vendor Lists on the BoM (Signature Edition)
name: Approved Vendor Lists on the BoM (Signature Edition)
title: Approved Vendor Lists on the BoM (Signature Edition)
